findings.title: .panel can be squeezed by long header content because it is a shrinkable flex item
findings.body: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container and `.panel` (the icons/login area) was changed from `float: right` to a flex item with `margin-left: auto` and `order: 3`. Floated blocks got a shrink-to-fit (max-content) width and never wrapped internally; a flex item defaults to `flex: 0 1 auto`, so when sibling content is wide the browser shrinks every item proportionally to its flex-basis. The `.extra-info-wrapper` sibling (order 2) carries the topic title, which can be hundreds of characters, so on topic pages with a long title the total max-content width exceeds the `.wrap` width and `.panel` loses a share of the overflow. `.panel`'s min-content width is only about one floated `li`/button wide, so its `.icons` and login/sign-up buttons wrap onto additional lines and the header grows taller. The icon panel needs `flex-shrink: 0` (or an explicit `flex: 0 0 auto`) so that only the title area absorbs the overflow, as it effectively did under the float layout.

findings.title: Float fallbacks removed, so browsers without flexbox now get a vertically stacked header
findings.body: The commit deletes `.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }` while adding the flex mixins. `float` is ignored on flex items, so keeping those declarations would have cost nothing in flex-capable browsers but would have preserved the horizontal logo-left/icons-right layout as a fallback in engines that ignore every `display: *flex*` value (IE9 and earlier, Opera Mini, older Android stock browsers in some modes). After this change those browsers render `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` as stacked full-width blocks. If those browsers are still in the support matrix, the float declarations should be retained alongside the mixin includes.

findings.title: align-items mixin passes modern keywords straight into legacy prefixed properties
findings.body: `@mixin align-items($alignment)` writes the same `$alignment` value to `-webkit-box-align` (2009 box syntax) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 syntax). Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any caller using `align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` will emit invalid declarations that old WebKit and IE10 silently drop, leaving the default `stretch` alignment there while modern browsers behave as requested. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline` (valid in all syntaxes), but this is a shared mixin introduced for general use and should map `flex-start`→`start` and `flex-end`→`end` for the prefixed outputs, as the standard flexbox-mixin snippets do.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms property and omits the -moz legacy equivalent
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version implemented (IE10 used `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 is unprefixed), so that line adds dead bytes to every rule that includes the mixin. Conversely, the `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -moz-box` and the `order()` mixin emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` has no `-moz-box-align`, so Firefox versions that fall into the `-moz-box` path get the ordering but never the alignment (they stay at the legacy default `stretch`). Either drop the `-moz-box` fallbacks consistently from all mixins or add `-moz-box-align` and remove `-ms-align-items`.

findings.title: PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and its description is just "Test 5". The diff replaces float-based positioning with flexbox and adds vendor-prefixed mixins; nothing in it targets layout or paint performance, and flexbox layout is not generally cheaper than floats. Anyone reading the history will be misled about why the header, small-action posts and category badges changed appearance. The title/description should describe the actual change (migrate header and small-action layout to flexbox, add prefixed flex mixins) and note the visual adjustments to `.small-action-desc` spacing and `.extra-info-wrapper`.
